problem_statement: Kuzma02/Fashion-eCommerce-Shop-in-React (rebranded here as the AURELIA couture storefront) is a Vite + React + Redux Toolkit single-page shop: a header wordmark with search / account / bag, a full-bleed banner, a home 'Our Collection' product grid, an 'Our Categories' block, and Shop, Single Product and Cart routes, all reading their catalog from an in-repo fixture. The storefront now carries a native 'Our Collection' finder: a row of house-category tabs (All pieces, Special Edition, Luxury Collection, Summer Edition, Unique Collection) that live-filters the product grid and shows a running 'Showing N of M · Label' result count, with an 'Add to bag' control on every card that increments the header bag badge ('Bag (N)'). The same finder heads the Shop and Single Product pages so the browse-and-add loop is consistent across the store. Your job: make the finder correct and robust on this storefront. (1) The category tabs must re-derive BOTH the shown grid AND the count readout live from the picked category, so the readout always matches the cards shown (e.g. picking Luxury Collection shows 'Showing 5 of 18 · Luxury Collection'). (2) 'Add to bag' must update the header bag badge immediately from the live cart. (3) The finder must be present at the head of the home, shop and single-product surfaces — not just the home page. (4) On a 390px mobile viewport the category row must wrap to fit with no horizontal overflow, and on desktop the product grid must lay out as a readable wrap of cards with legible, high-contrast labels — never a single overlapping/clipped row or near-invisible text. Keep the header wordmark, banner, categories block, footer, and the Shop / Single Product / Cart routes intact, and introduce no new console errors or failed network requests.
required_content: The 'Our Collection' finder renders the same five house-category tabs (All pieces, Special Edition, Luxury Collection, Summer Edition, Unique Collection) and, when a category is picked, re-derives BOTH the shown product cards and the 'Showing N of M · Label' count readout live from that category (picking Luxury Collection yields 'Showing 5 of 18 · Luxury Collection' with five cards shown).
Each product card carries an 'Add to bag' control that adds the piece to the cart and updates the header bag badge to 'Bag (1)' (and upward) immediately from the live cart state.

The finder heads the home page, the Shop page and the Single Product page — the category tabs and 'Our Collection' heading appear on all three surfaces, and the bag badge appears in the header on every route.

On a 390px mobile viewport the home page has no horizontal overflow beyond a small tolerance: the category tab row wraps to fit the screen instead of forcing the document wider than the viewport, in both the initial and the filtered state.

On desktop the product grid lays out as a readable wrap of cards with legible, high-contrast titles, prices and category labels; cards never collapse into a single overlapping/clipped row and text is never near-invisible on its background.

The header wordmark, banner, 'Our Categories' block, footer and the Shop / Single Product / Cart routes remain present and unchanged in content and structure, with no new console errors or failed network requests.
design_constraints: Preserve the AURELIA storefront visual style: an ink-on-cream palette with the warm secondaryBrown (#6b5844) accent for the active tab and the add-to-bag button; do not introduce an off-brand slate/grey wash or low-contrast theme on the finder.

The finder is a native layout section of each browse surface (home / shop / product), placed directly above the product grid it controls with consistent spacing — it is not a floating decorative strip.

Category tabs are pill buttons that wrap on narrow / mobile viewports (flex-wrap) so the row is responsive and self-clamps; the product grid is a responsive flex wrap of fixed-max-width cards with even spacing, never a nowrap row with negative margins that overlaps or clips cards.

Each card keeps its product image, title, price and category label legible with strong typography and contrast; the count readout and header bag badge are plain, high-contrast text derived from live state, never near-invisible on their background.
Maintain visual consistency with the existing header, banner, categories block and footer layout so the finder reads as part of the same storefront style.
state_constraints: desktop_initial captures the storefront home at 1440px: header (with bag badge 'Bag (0)'), banner and the 'Our Collection' finder (five category tabs + 'Showing all 18 pieces' readout + product grid) all fit with no horizontal overflow.
desktop_home_filtered clicks the Luxury Collection tab: the grid re-renders to the five luxury pieces and the readout reads 'Showing 5 of 18 · Luxury Collection'.
desktop_home_added clicks 'Add to bag' on the first card: the header badge updates to 'Bag (1)'.
mobile_initial and mobile_home_filtered capture the 390px home before/after filtering: the category tab row wraps with no horizontal overflow.
desktop_shop and desktop_product capture the Shop and Single Product pages: the finder heads each and the bag badge stays in the header.
desktop_cart captures the cart route with the header badge intact.

change_completion: Clicking a category tab re-derives both the shown grid and the 'Showing N of M · Label' readout live from the picked category (Luxury Collection -> 'Showing 5 of 18 · Luxury Collection', five cards).
'Add to bag' updates the header bag badge to 'Bag (1)' and upward from the live cart state.
design_consistency: The finder uses the ink-on-cream AURELIA palette with the secondaryBrown accent; active tabs and labels are legible and high-contrast.
The finder is a native section above the product grid on every browse surface, not a floating strip.
responsive: On a 390px mobile viewport the category tab row wraps to fit with no horizontal overflow beyond tolerance, in both the initial and filtered states — the mobile layout stays responsive.
At 1440px desktop and 834px tablet the finder and product grid lay out cleanly with no horizontal overflow and no card overlap.
regression: The existing header wordmark, banner, 'Our Categories' block, footer and the Shop / Single Product / Cart routes remain present and unchanged in content and structure.
No new console errors or failed network requests are introduced; the build remains a self-contained static SPA reading the existing in-repo fixture.

author_notes: Repo-grounded extend_interaction / experience_continuity task on the Vite + React + Redux Toolkit Kuzma02 Fashion-eCommerce-Shop-in-React SPA (AURELIA storefront). The native lever is the store's own 'Our Collection' product-grid category finder (tabs + live 'Showing N of M · Label' count) plus the header shopping-bag badge — both real commerce controls placed where the genre hosts them. Four orthogonal gates: D6 mobile overflow of the category tab row, D3 visual regression of the finder (shingled/clipped grid + illegible near-white labels), D2 cross-page presence of the finder across the home / shop / single-product surfaces, D4 interaction on the filter readout and the bag badge. Assets: product image 1.jpg, luxury category 1.png, banner assets and the db.json catalog fixture. The baseline reuses the correct finder wiring (passes D4) with only a broken stylesheet; the bad leg snapshots the filter/badge and drops the finder from the secondary pages so it fails all four gates.

metadata.selected_repo_reason: Kuzma02/Fashion-eCommerce-Shop-in-React is a runnable Vite + React + Redux Toolkit ecommerce SPA (header with bag icon, banner, home collection grid, categories, shop, single product, cart) reading its catalog from an in-repo fixture. It natively hosts a product-grid category filter with a result count and a header bag badge, making it an ideal host for an extend_interaction / experience_continuity task whose four orthogonal discriminators are mobile overflow, finder visual regression, cross-page finder presence and the filter/bag interactions.

design_charter.q1_genre_and_native_lever: Genre: a fashion e-commerce storefront (React + Redux). The native lever is the store's own product-grid category filter with a live result count PLUS the header shopping-bag badge — the two controls a commerce site genuinely hosts. Neither is a bolted-on metric strip; the finder sits above the 'Our Collection' grid it filters, and the badge lives on the existing bag icon in the header.
design_charter.q2_where_genre_hosts_it: Storefronts host the category filter directly above the product grid and the bag count on the header cart icon. We keep exactly those placements: the finder heads 'Our Collection' on home and repeats above the grid on the Shop and Single Product pages; the badge is the existing header bag link.
design_charter.q3_d4_control_and_bad_bug: D4 is two real controls: (a) clicking a category tab re-derives the shown cards and the 'Showing N of M · Label' readout; (b) 'Add to bag' increments the header badge. The bad leg snapshots both the filtered set/readout (useState(()=>...) at mount) and the badge label at first render, so clicks still flip the active pill and dispatch to the store (the interaction registers) but the readout stays 'Showing all 18 pieces' and the badge stays 'Bag (0)'.
design_charter.q4_d3_credible_defect: The bad grid is forced into a single nowrap row with large negative right margins so the cards shingle over each other and the last cards shear off the viewport, and the finder head + tab labels are set to near-white on near-white so the title, readout and category labels are illegible. A designer would reject it on sight — it is an overlap + clip + contrast failure, not a palette swap.
design_charter.q5_d2_cross_page: The finder is registered per surface (home / shop / product). Reference and baseline register all three; the bad leg registers only 'home', so the finder is absent on the Shop and Single Product pages while the bag badge (header) stays everywhere.
design_charter.q6_d6_mobile_break: The bad and baseline category rows use flex-wrap:nowrap with a fixed 680px min-width and margin:0 (no margin:auto self-clamp), so at 390px the row pushes the document to ~844px wide (about 454px overflow). The reference row wraps and measures about 0.
design_charter.q7_leg_orthogonality: Baseline copies the reference finder/badge wiring verbatim (correct D4) and only its layout stylesheet is broken (fixed nowrap tabs + off-brand wash), so baseline fails D6+D3+D2 but PASSES D4 — proving D4 is orthogonal to the layout gates. Bad breaks all four.
design_charter.q8_infra_identical: The offline catalog fixture (axios shim + db.json), the FinderMount wrapper, the Landing/Shop/SingleProduct integration and the product copy are byte-identical across all three legs. Only the CollectionFinder component, its stylesheet, the Header, and the surface-presence registry differ per leg.
design_charter.q9_quality_watch: The reference filter genuinely filters to the picked category and the readout label matches the shown cards (Luxury Collection -> 5 of 18). No canvas/3d/shader wording. Lorem-ipsum product copy replaced with real atelier copy across all legs.
